note.text:
A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers in rows and columns, written in brackets.
• Its order is (number of rows) × (number of columns): a matrix with 2 rows and 3 columns is 2 × 3.
• Each number is an element; aᵢⱼ is the element in row i, column j.
• Types: row matrix (one row), column matrix (one column), square matrix (rows = columns), zero matrix (all zeros), diagonal matrix (zeros off the leading diagonal), identity matrix I (ones on the leading diagonal, zeros elsewhere).
• Two matrices are equal when they have the same order and equal corresponding elements.

sections.heading: What a matrix is
sections.text:
A matrix is a table of numbers in rows and columns, written inside brackets. A shop in Limbe might record sales of bread and milk on Monday and Tuesday in a matrix: each row a day, each column a product.
Rows go across (left to right). Columns go down (top to bottom).

sections.heading: Order and elements
sections.text:
The order of a matrix is rows × columns, always rows first. A matrix with {2} rows and {3} columns has order {2} × {3} and {6} elements.
Each number is an element. We name it by its row and column: a₁₂ is the element in row {1}, column {2}.
In S above, s₂₁ = {9}: row {2} (Tuesday), column {1} (bread).

sections.heading: Special matrices
sections.text:
• Row matrix: one row, like {matStr([[3, 1, 4]])}.
• Column matrix: one column.
• Square matrix: as many rows as columns.
• Zero matrix: every element {0}.
• Diagonal matrix: square, zero except on the leading diagonal (top left to bottom right).
• Identity matrix I: diagonal with every diagonal element {1}, like {matStr([[1, 0], [0, 1]])}. It behaves like the number {1} in multiplication.

questions.prompt: What type of matrix is A?
Matrices P and Q are equal. Find x.
solution: Equal matrices have equal corresponding elements.

questions.prompt: A matrix has {m * n} elements arranged in {m} rows. How many columns does it have?

misconceptions.explain: {m} is the number of rows. Divide the elements by the rows.
{m * n} is the number of elements.

solution: {m * n} = {m} × columns, so there are {answer} columns. Its order is {m} × {n}.
